findings.issue_text: [BUG] embed.css.scss uses dark-light-choose() and $secondary, which are theme-color SCSS definitions that the embed stylesheet compilation pipeline does not provide. The embed stylesheet is compiled through a separate pipeline (Stylesheet compiler for /embed.css) that does not inject the theme color variables or the dark-light-choose() function the way the main admin/common/desktop/mobile bundles get them via color scheme imports; compilation fails with 'undefined function dark-light-choose' (or undefined variable $secondary), breaking embedded topic rendering on any site using a custom color scheme. Every other file in this diff is part of the theme-aware bundle; this one is not.

[ADVISORY] The dark-theme branch for this link uses lightness 70% where every sibling change in the PR inverts the light theme value (30% dark-becomes-light 70%), producing a dark-mode value that no longer matches the intended visual weight. Users of dark themes get links styled at a different visual weight than light-theme users at the same site; also suggests a copy-paste error that the next maintainer will silently propagate. Rebuttal (author may have intentionally matched adjacent 50% values) fails because the light-mode value was left at 30%, breaking the inversion pattern the PR title claims.

[ADVISORY] mobile/modal.scss .custom-message-length dark branch is inverted relative to the desktop/modal.scss counterpart (primary 30%/secondary 70% here vs primary 70%/secondary 30% on desktop). Mobile dark-theme users see the message-length hint at full-strength color while desktop dark users see it muted; the two parallel hand-maintained rules have drifted in the same PR, so a future fix will have to remember both sites. Rebuttal (intentional mobile-specific contrast) fails because no other mobile/desktop pair in this diff diverges in polarity.

[BUG] The light-theme branch was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), altering light-theme rendering instead of only adding a dark-theme alternative. On light themes, the small-action link text (.small-action a, e.g. 'posted, closed' action links) renders at 70% lightness instead of the previous 30%, becoming washed out and low-contrast; this is a regression on the untouched (light) side of the change.

[BUG] The light-theme value of .custom-message-length was flipped from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) while converting it, changing light-theme behavior. On light themes the custom message length hint in modals now renders at 30% lightness (much darker than the previous 70%) instead of the intended dim hint styling, diverging from the desktop counterpart at desktop/modal.scss:93-95 which correctly keeps 70%.

[ADVISORY] The .name color was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) in the light branch, silently weakening light-theme contrast and diverging from mobile/user.scss:497 where the same 30%->50% flip also occurred. User full names in the message below user cards render lighter (50% vs 30%) on light themes, reducing the visual hierarchy between bold username and name that the original 30% established.

[ADVISORY] The h3 (small-action title) light-branch lightness was changed from 20% to 50% during the conversion, diverging from desktop/topic-post.scss:321 which retains 20% for the same selector. Mobile users on light themes see small-action titles at half the previous contrast, and mobile/desktop now disagree for the identical component, indicating a copy-paste conversion error rather than an intentional design change.

[ADVISORY] The disabled reply-title and wmd-input background uses dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 75%), scale-color($secondary, 25%)), but the adjacent .wmd-input rule sets text color to darken($primary, 40%) with no dark-light-choose, so on dark themes disabled inputs keep a dark-primary-derived text color that has no dark-theme counterpart. Dark-theme users see disabled compose inputs whose background (secondary at 25% lightness) can make the darken($primary, 40%) text unreadable; the sibling rule on the same rendering path was left unconverted.

[ADVISORY] The converted light-branch uses $lightness: 10% for figure text, but the desktop equivalent and most sibling conversions in this diff use 50% for metadata text; a 10%-lightness primary is nearly black on light themes and the paired dark value 90% makes $secondary nearly white on dark themes, both extreme for a caption. Category featured-topic figure captions render at extreme contrast on both themes (near-black on light, near-white on dark), visually shouting small caption text; likely a mis-transcribed value given the surrounding conversions use moderate values.

[ADVISORY] No test or visual-verification artifact accompanies this cross-cutting dark-theme conversion of ~80 color rules across 30 stylesheets; the diff contains zero spec/test files. The light-branch value flips (topic-post.scss:291, mobile/modal.scss:102, user.scss .name) ship undetected because no regression check compares pre/post light-theme computed colors; the actual Discourse PR history shows this class of conversion error requires manual visual review that this diff omits.

[BUG] The nested-post author link lightens the light-theme color from 30% to 70% lightness while wrapping it in dark-light-choose, changing light-theme appearance outside the PR's stated intent. Light-theme users see reply-author names at 70% lightness (nearly invisible against a white background) instead of the previous 30%, a light-mode regression not traceable to the 'dark themes use $secondary' requirement.

[BUG] The .name rule's light-theme lightness is changed from 30% to 50% while being wrapped, mutating the light-mode value instead of only adding the dark-theme branch. Light-theme user profile names become washed out at 50% lightness; the PR is titled as dark-theme-only, so this light-mode change is scope drift with no requirement tracing to it.

[BUG] The small-action h3 lightness is changed from 20% to 50% in the light-mode argument of dark-light-choose, altering light-theme styling beyond the stated intent. Mobile light-theme h3 headings lose their previous strong 20%-lightness contrast and render at 50%, a light-mode regression unrelated to the dark-theme requirement.

[BUG] The .name rule's light-theme lightness is changed from 30% to 50%, modifying the light-mode value rather than only adding a dark-theme alternative. Mobile light-theme user names drop from 30% to 50% lightness contrast; this light-mode change is not traceable to the PR's dark-theme-only intent.

[ADVISORY] The mobile .custom-message-length light-theme lightness is changed from 70% to 30%, diverging from the parallel desktop/modal.scss rule which keeps 70%/30% (light/dark). Mobile light-theme users get a nearly-black custom-message-length hint while desktop keeps the muted 70% tone; the parallel implementations drift, so the next change to one will miss the other.

[ADVISORY] The adjacent .wmd-input color uses darken($primary, 40%) and is left untouched, so the same disabled-editor block now mixes a dark-light-choose background with a raw darken() text color that goes unmigrated. Dark-theme users get disabled composer input with the new $secondary-based background but still darken($primary, 40%) text — darkened primary on dark secondary yields near-black-on-dark text; under-scoping leaves an inconsistent dark-theme rendering in the same visual block the PR touched.

[ADVISORY] The comment above the coldmap rules still asserts the canonical muted color 'is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)' while the diff converts every such usage to dark-light-choose, leaving the comment and code contradictory. The next developer touching heat/cold map colors reads the comment, follows the documented pattern, and reintroduces the dark-theme bug this PR fixes; the stated invariant is no longer documented anywhere after the migration.

[BUG] The light-theme branch of .custom-message-length was silently changed from $primary lightness 70% to 30%, breaking the light theme as well as the intended dark-theme-only change. On light themes the mobile custom-message-length hint text (character counter in modals) renders much darker than before this diff; the desktop/modal.scss:91 counterpart keeps 70%, so mobile and desktop visually diverge for the same element. The correct change was dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 70%), scale-color($secondary, 30%)).

[BUG] The light-theme value of this a{font-weight:bold} rule (small-action/nav link block) was changed from scale-color($primary, 30%) to scale-color($primary, 70%), altering light-theme rendering instead of only adding the dark-theme branch. On light themes these bold small-action links become far lighter/washed out; every sibling conversion in this diff preserves the original lightness value, so this one is a transcription error (30 and 70 swapped).

[BUG] The .name rule's light-theme value was changed from $primary 30% to 50% while converting to dark-light-choose, an unintended change to light-theme styling. On light themes the user profile .name is now lighter than before, losing the intended 30%-vs-50% contrast with the adjacent .title rule three lines below (which kept 50%); name and title now render identically instead of hierarchy-differentiated.

[BUG] The .name rule's light-theme value was changed from $primary 30% to 50% during conversion, diverging from its desktop counterpart and from the pre-diff light-theme value. On light themes the mobile user profile .name loses its darker 30% emphasis and now matches .title exactly, collapsing the visual hierarchy; desktop/user.scss has the identical transcription error so the two are consistently wrong rather than visibly divergent, making it harder to notice.

[BUG] The h3 (small-action heading) light-theme value was changed from $primary 20% to 50%, altering light-theme appearance instead of only adding the dark branch. On light themes the mobile small-action h3 becomes significantly lighter than the pre-diff 20%; the desktop counterpart (desktop/topic-post.scss:321) correctly preserves 20%, so mobile and desktop now render this heading differently on light themes.

[ADVISORY] The coldmap classes are converted to dark-light-choose but hardcode hex literals (#fe7a15 etc.) for heatmap in the same block, leaving the heat/cold map only half theme-aware. Dark-theme users get adaptive coldmap text but heatmap text remains fixed-lightness orange/gold, producing inconsistent contrast within the same heatmap widget; whoever finishes the conversion later must rediscover this block.

[BUG] The light-theme branch value was changed from 30% to 70% lightness, altering light-theme appearance instead of only adding a dark-theme fallback. Users on light themes see the .names a/bold link inside post timeline rows rendered 40% lighter than before this PR — a visual regression in the shipped light theme that no one accepted, since the PR's stated intent is only to fix dark themes.

[BUG] The light-theme branch of .custom-message-length was changed from 70% to 30% lightness, silently changing light-theme styling. Mobile users on light themes see the custom message length counter text drastically darker than before; every other site in this PR keeps the light value identical, so this is unintended intent drift, and it also diverges from desktop/modal.scss line ~94 which keeps 70%.

[BUG] The light-theme branch for the user card .name was changed from 30% to 50% lightness, modifying light-theme styling beyond the PR's stated scope. Desktop light-theme users see the profile .name text lighter (less prominent) than before; this is a light-theme behavior change smuggled into a dark-theme-only PR and not covered by any review intent.

[BUG] The light-theme branch for the mobile user card .name was changed from 30% to 50% lightness. Mobile light-theme users see the profile .name lose its previous emphasis; same unintended light-theme change as desktop/user.scss, indicating a copy of an incorrect value rather than the original 30%.

[BUG] The light-theme branch for the mobile external-link h3 was changed from 20% to 50% lightness, altering light-theme styling. Mobile light-theme users see the link preview title far lighter than before, a silent visual regression in the light theme; desktop/topic-post.scss line ~320 correctly keeps 20% for the same element, producing desktop/mobile divergence.

[ADVISORY] dark-light-choose() is used in embed.css.scss, which compiles as a standalone stylesheet with a restricted import set; if the function is not defined in the embed SCSS import chain the stylesheet fails to compile, and if it is defined via a different logic path the embedded dark-theme output may differ from the main app. Embedded comments (third-party sites) either break asset compilation after deploy or render colors inconsistent with the accepted main-app dark-theme mapping; either way this line needs explicit verification that the function resolves in the embed build.

Thus the finding misreads what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The mobile .custom-message-length light-theme lightness is changed from 70% to 30%, diverging from the parallel desktop/modal.scss rule which keeps 70%/30% (light/dark). adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss`, `.custom-message-length` was changed to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, making the light-theme (first argument) use 30% lightness. In the parallel desktop rule (`app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/modal.scss`), it uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. This is a clear divergence introduced by the diff and will make mobile light-theme styling much darker than desktop for the same hint text, indicating a likely UI regression/inconsistency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] dark-light-choose() is used in embed.css.scss, which compiles as a standalone stylesheet with a restricted import set; if the function is not defined in the embed SCSS import chain the stylesheet fails to compile, and if it is defined via a different logic path the embedded dark-theme output may differ from the main app. Embedded comments (third-party sites) either break asset compilation after deploy or render colors inconsistent with the accepted main-app dark-theme mapping; either way this line needs explicit verification that the function resolves in the embed build.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` to use `dark-light-choose(...)` (e.g., `a.new-user { color: dark-light-choose(...) }`). The finding’s concern is about whether `dark-light-choose()` is available in the embed stylesheet’s standalone compilation/import context; that import chain is not shown in this diff, so an actual compile break or theme inconsistency cannot be verified from the provided changes alone. Still, it is a concrete, diff-triggered risk that warrants explicit verification.
